approaches.name: integrated 911 platform merging emergency and GBV hotlines
approaches.description: The project integrates firefighter, SAMU and Line 100 GBV hotline systems into one interoperable 911 platform with geolocation, outsourced operation and maintenance. Practices: Integrated 911 platform merging emergency and GBV hotlines; Line 100 digital system integrated into 911 Platform; 911-to-GBV Line 100 call transfer and tracking; private-sector outsourcing of 911 platform O&M; interoperable 911 communications system for multi-agency first response.

evidence.text: The proposed project will seek to integrate the three key emergency response numbers mentioned above (NPP, PCVF, and SAMU) as they are the ones receiving approximately 90 percent of the calls and will progressively include the remaining emergency numbers as described in annex 2.

extra_evidence.text: The existing emergency response numbers (105, 106, and 116) will be phased out gradually, and all calls made to the First Response Units will be automatically transferred to the 911 system.

Lines 100 and 911 will coexist, and all calls made to Line 100 will access the 911 system to benefit from receiving (a) alerts of previous malicious calls, (b) automatic information of previous emergency calls, and (c) the geolocation of calls.

The following activities will improve the delivery of services offered by Line 100, as well as a more coordinated and efficient response in case of GBV emergencies or urgencies: (a) the integration of the Line 100 digital system to the 911 Platform, aiming at reducing malicious calls and response times;

O&M of the centralized emergency response platform will be done entirely by the private sector.

Furthermore, the implementation and O&M of the 911 service will be transferred and may be awarded to one or more specialized national or international companies, following the contracting modalities provided in the applicable national regulations according to Article 38 of the referred Supreme Decree.

The efficiency gain is greater when the incident requires more agencies to coordinate, largely due to the interoperable 911 system which will enable faster communication and better coordination between First Response Units.

There are two aspects of the efficiency gains from the proposed project, reduced response time from (a) implementing a real-time and immediate geolocation of the calls and (b) better interagency coordination through a centralized system.
On average, the response time during 2020–2030 will be reduced by seven minutes after implementing the centralized emergency response.

approaches.name: interoperable 911 platform with geolocation, caller profiling and analytics
approaches.description: An open-standards 911 platform auto-geolocates calls, profiles and blacklists callers, links SAMU and early-warning systems, and analyzes call data for planning. evidence.text: This will be done by (a) establishing an integrated communications platform, (b) adopting specific and well-coordinated emergency response protocols and procedures, (c) promoting the linking of the recently implemented Early Warning Messaging System ( Sistema de Mensajería de Alerta Temprana de Emergencia, SISMATE) with the 911 system, and (d) providing much-needed capacity building.

extra_evidence.text: It will include a geolocation system that will allow automatic geolocation of calls received by the 911 Center.
The 911 Platform will receive, categorize, transfer, and perform the traceability of the calls that are sent to the First Response Units.
In addition, the platform will, at minimum, automatically (a) geolocate the call;

(b) alert if the incoming number has made malicious calls in the past; and (c) display all available profile and background information of the caller, including records of any previous calls made by that caller.

The 911 Platform will also enable data analytics and planning of future emergency response, identification of high-risk areas, and potential solutions to reduce the risk of emergencies or disasters in the future.
The PRONATEL PIU met with them to discuss synergies and opportunities for collaboration, and to promote interoperability between the systems used by the SAMU first response units and the 911 Center.

The PRONATEL PIU will coordinate with the MoH PIU when defining the technical specifications of the 911 Platform to promote the interoperability of the system that will be implemented in the new medical center with the 911 Platform.
To ensure replicability the 911 Platform will be developed using open standards.
The project is focused on the regions of the Lima Metropolitan area and Callao and is considered the first phase of a national roll-out.
